episode_title: 5 Leading Indicators Every Business Owner Must Track
question: What is the difference between leading indicators and lagging metrics in e-commerce business management?
transcript_excerpt: A lagging metric in business is your profit and your revenue, which are at least six-month lagging indicators. Leading indicators are the actions and measurable activities that predict future results. For example, in media buying on Meta, leading indicators include the number of new ad concepts created, AI videos produced, static images created, and winning ads identified. If these leading indicators are green, you can confidently predict positive results in profitability a month ahead.

episode_title: 5 Leading Indicators Every Business Owner Must Track
question: What are the five key leading indicators Josh Hadley tracks weekly in his e-commerce business?
transcript_excerpt: Josh Hadley reviews a weekly report called the High Five Tracker every Monday, where each team member has five leading actions or indicators being measured. For media buying specifically, these include: the number of new customer avatar variations or winning ads (KPI of 10 per week), new AI videos produced (KPI of 100), new static images produced (KPI of 50), and at least three winning ads identified in the account to double down on. If all metrics are green, he can predict positive results in media buying profitability the following week.

episode_title: 5 Leading Indicators Every Business Owner Must Track
question: How did Josh Hadley discover a major inventory problem despite all leading indicators showing green?
transcript_excerpt: Josh Hadley discovered a critical mismatch when all leading indicators and supply chain metrics appeared green, yet his balance sheet showed inventory growing faster than sales year over year. He flagged this disconnect to his department head and director of operations, realizing that inventory growth outpacing sales growth is a major problem in e-commerce. This discovery led him to fundamentally change his inventory management and supply chain processes.

episode_title: 5 Leading Indicators Every Business Owner Must Track
question: Why did Thrasio go bankrupt and what role did inventory play in the collapse?
transcript_excerpt: Thrasio went bankrupt not only due to poor execution but primarily because they massively overpurchased inventory. They ended up with five to ten years worth of inventory and even twenty years worth of inventory on certain SKUs because they did not have good processes, checks and balances, or the right operating system in place. This demonstrates why inventory is described as the kryptonite for e-commerce brands and how poor inventory management is where the best brands go to die.

episode_title: 5 Leading Indicators Every Business Owner Must Track
question: What should e-commerce business owners do monthly to avoid flying blind in their operations?
transcript_excerpt: Business owners should review their profit and loss statement every single month and measure leading indicators alongside lagging metrics together. Josh Hadley emphasizes that if you are not conducting a monthly financial review with whoever produces your P&L, you will start flying blind. This monthly review allows you to catch disconnects between green leading indicators and negative lagging metrics before they become major problems.
